Jaimini
ancient authority on Mīm. According to tradition he was born in Dvaitavana (Deoband) an. was a. student of Bādarāyaṇa (a. of Brahmasūtras); Jaimini an. Bādarāyaṇa refer to each other, perhaps indicating contemporaneity of redaction of both Sūtras. One Jaimini is ref. to in Āśval. gṛh. sūtra III. iii. 5. According to Kumārilabhaṭṭa, Tantravārttika on I. iii. 2 (5), Jaimini is the a. of Chāndogyānuvāda (etajjaimininaiva chAndogyAnuvAde). A gṛh. sūtra an. a.śr. śūtra are generally ascribed to him; but Jaiminīya or Talavakāra is one of the śākhās of Sv. an. works belonging to this school are known a. Jaimini's. Many later works like Jaiminibhārata (Jaiminīyāśvamedha) an. Jaiminisūtra (jy.) are ascribed to him. On different Jaiminis see K. A. Nilakantha Sastri, Ind.

, p.. 167 ff.
